t: An aristocratic merchant republic centred on Dubrovnik, independent in practice from 1358 to 1808.
It traded Balkan silver and lead and had one of the largest merchant fleets in the Mediterranean in the 16th century.
It kept its freedom by paying tribute to the Ottomans, staying neutral and governing itself through noble councils.
dyk: The Rector of Ragusa served for just one month and could not leave his palace during that time except on official business, so that no one could gain personal power.
ev: The city statute codifies Ragusan law
The Treaty of Zadar ends Venetian rule; Ragusa becomes a self-governing republic
Ragusa introduces quarantine regulations for travellers from infected areas
The Great Council bans the slave trade
Ragusa begins paying tribute to the Ottoman Empire
A great earthquake destroys much of the city
The Treaty of Karlowitz creates Ottoman corridors separating Ragusa from Venice

f.successor: French Empire (Illyrian Provinces); later the Austrian Empire
